content: Anti-inflammatory substances or treatments are those that reduce inflammation in the body. These are commonly used in medical practice to manage pain and inflammation. Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs Steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, particularly glucocorticoids, work by binding to cortisol receptors, thereby reducing inflammation. These drugs are often referred to as corticosteroids, although corticosteroids encompass a broader category of substances. Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs) Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) alleviate pain by inhibiting the cyclooxygenase (COX) enzyme. The COX enzyme is responsible for synthesizing prostaglandins, which are compounds that promote inflammation. By preventing the synthesis of prostaglandins, NSAIDs effectively reduce or eliminate pain. However, long-term use of NSAIDs can lead to gastric erosions, which may progress to stomach ulcers and, in severe cases, result in death. The risk of death from NSAID use is approximately 1 in 10,000 for young adults aged 16–45, but this risk increases tenfold in individuals over the age of 75. Ice Treatment Applying ice to an injured tissue has an anti-inflammatory effect and is often recommended as a treatment for injuries and pain management, particularly for athletes. However, practitioners of Chinese medicine argue that ice is only beneficial within the first 24 hours following acute trauma. Beyond this period, ice may hinder the healing process by inhibiting local blood circulation. Anti-inflammatory Foods Due to concerns about the gastric side effects of NSAIDs, researchers are exploring natural alternatives for managing inflammation. Capsaicin, a naturally occurring compound in chili peppers, has shown promise in controlling pain and inflammation when applied topically. Additionally, consuming anti-inflammatory foods is advocated as a means of managing inflammation. These foods include colorful fruits and vegetables, oily fish, and certain nuts, seeds, herbs, and spices such as ginger. An anti-inflammatory diet typically avoids refined oils and sugars, favoring anti-inflammatory food choices instead. Other Considerations Tobacco may have some anti-inflammatory effects, as noted in the Smoker’s Paradox. Furthermore, dietary omega-3 fatty acids have been shown to reduce inflammation in certain conditions, as seen in studies on essential fatty acid interactions.
